digest.component_or_area: transition request / close-reason/force plumbing across CLI, library, and MCP
propositions: close-reason and force plumbing is duplicated across three surfaces (transition.py:584, _lib_writes.py:318, txn.py:357-362) with inconsistent naming (force_reason → force_close → force_close_reason) and differing refusal behavior (CLI refuses, library silently discards)
MCP transition_ticket does not expose reason parameter, causing strict-xfail in write-parity-contract test, while CLI and library handle it

the '(no reason given)' placeholder literal is produced in five code sites across three files with no single point of control, violating the principle that a normalized datum should have one production source

CLI refuses an inadmissible close-reason with exit 1 while library silently discards it (returns 0), and both behaviors are pinned by tests, creating an asymmetry that blocks convergence via any single shared implementation

a bare --force close (empty force_reason) works only because force-note normalization happens before the reason-requirement check at txn.py:232, making the order of normalization relative to refusal checks load-bearing
the placeholder must never reach close_disposition.verdict because it would transform an UNJUSTIFIED disposition into a SIGNED one by providing a non-empty reason
